newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Two Chinese firms in Hong Kong derivatives trading.
newsitem.headline: Two Chinese firms in Hong Kong derivatives trading.

text.p: Hong Kong stock exchange and future exchange said on Tuesday trading in stock options and stock futures on the shares of two China-affiliated corporation would begin on July 14.
The two exchanges said in a joint statement that two companies were China Resources Enterprises Ltd and Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd.
The statement said the two firms were the first non-Hang Seng Index component companies to have exchange traded stock options and stock futures introduced on their shares.

The introduction of derivatives on the shares of China Resources and Shanghai Industrial brought the number of stock options classes traded at the stock exchange to 15, and the number of stock futures contracts traded at the future exchange to seven.
It also said trading in derivatives contracts had increased significantly in recent months at both exchanges.

In June, open interest in stock options reached a record of more than 240,000 contracts, while at the future exchange, Hang Seng Index Futures achieved a record volume of 500,746 contracts traded in May.

The statement added the futures exchange's Hang Seng Index Options Contract, with May volume of 128,710 contracts, continued as the most popular and fastest growing exchange traded equity index options contract in Asia, excluding Japan.
